"""Parser-based TOML/JSON/YAML structured-reference codemod (P02S).

Rewrites identity references (e.g. an old repository slug substring) that
appear inside *string scalar values* of TOML, JSON, and YAML documents,
using a real format-specific parser for each format rather than regex or
line-oriented text substitution. Never touches:

- mapping/table/object **keys** (only values are ever rewritten);
- comments (TOML/YAML only; JSON has none);
- content wrapped in a YAML tag this tool does not recognise.

Safety model
------------
For every input file this tool first parses the file, then immediately
serialises the *unmodified* parsed tree back to text ("control round-trip").
If that control text is not byte-identical to the original source, the
file is refused (``round_trip_fidelity_unsupported``, severity ``unsafe``):
this tool will not silently re-format content it cannot prove it can
reproduce exactly. Only once the control round-trip is proven exact does
it proceed to apply the requested string replacements and re-serialise.

This is the single mechanism that satisfies "preserve formatting ... to
the degree supported by the selected format-specific parser; when safe
round-trip preservation is impossible, fail with an actionable diagnostic
rather than falling back to regex."

Pinned parsers
---------------
- TOML: ``tomlkit`` (format-preserving TOML parser/writer).
- YAML: ``ruamel.yaml`` in round-trip mode (``typ="rt"``), with quote
  preservation and auto-detected block-sequence indentation.
- JSON: the standard library ``json`` module, with an auto-detected
  indent width / trailing-newline / ``ensure_ascii`` profile reproduced
  on output, and a custom ``object_pairs_hook`` that rejects duplicate
  keys (which the JSON grammar permits but which are almost always a
  defect).

Exact versions are asserted at import time (see ``_assert_pinned_versions``)
so an unpinned/drifted environment fails loudly instead of silently
producing different output on a different machine.
"""
